odeComponent.htmlView:
Welcome to the "Savouring Science" Challenge! 🥗🧪

Have you ever wondered why fast-food logos are often red and yellow? Or why some flavours make your mouth water while others are simply "meh"?

In this project, you are not just English students; you are Food Scientists and Designers. Your mission is to create a digital menu that is not only delicious but scientifically engineered to trigger emotions and cravings using the Psychology of Colour and the Science of Taste.

The Final Goal: Design a professional menu in Canva that uses the First Conditional to tempt your customers and demonstrates your mastery of sensory vocabulary.

Are you ready to cook up some science?

In Savouring Science, we work with digital tools like Padlet and Canva to share our findings and collaborate with peers.

However, just as we follow safety protocols in a science lab to avoid accidents, we must follow Digital Safety protocols to protect our identity and digital footprint.

In this section, we will learn how to:

Collaborate safely: Sharing ideas without revealing personal sensitive data.

Respect Intellectual Property: Always citing our sources and using Creative Commons resources (like we do in this project!).

Manage our Digital Footprint: Being aware that what we post today in our collaborative walls contributes to our online reputation in the future.

Remember: A great scientist not only discovers the truth but also communicates it ethically and safely.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Diseño de "Sensory Menus" con Canva (Proyecto Savouring Science)

1. Herramienta digital propuesta: Canva para Educación.

2. Objetivo de usar esta herramienta: El objetivo es que el alumnado materialice la fase creativa de la unidad mediante el diseño de un menú interactivo. Deben aplicar los conocimientos científicos adquiridos sobre la psicología del gusto para diseñar tres platos, justificando sus elecciones sensoriales mediante el uso del First Conditional (ej: "If I use blue plates, the food will look less appetizing").

3. Justificación de la elección:

Versatilidad: Canva permite pasar de una simple plantilla de menú a un producto profesional que integra imágenes, iconos y elementos gráficos que refuerzan el mensaje visual de su investigación.
Contexto y disponibilidad: El centro cuenta con cuentas corporativas, lo que permite al alumnado acceder a las funciones avanzadas de la herramienta de forma gratuita y bajo un entorno seguro que garantiza la protección de datos.
Edad y características del alumnado: Los alumnos de 3º de ESO responden mejor a la gramática cuando se presenta como un desafío técnico y creativo. Esta herramienta minimiza las barreras de diseño, permitiéndoles centrarse en la producción lingüística en inglés y en la organización lógica de sus argumentos científicos.
Accesibilidad: He seleccionado esta opción porque ofrece herramientas integradas para verificar el contraste de colores (esencial para alumnos con baja visión) y permite añadir texto alternativo a las imágenes. Esto asegura que el producto final sea inclusivo y pueda ser procesado por lectores de pantalla, adaptándose a la diversidad del aula.

To achieve our goal of designing a professional sensory menu, we will follow a structured timeline. This roadmap ensures that we balance scientific research, linguistic practice, and creative design.

The project is divided into four main stages:

Exploration: Researching the psychology of colour and the science of taste using our collaborative Padlet.
The Grammar Challenge: Master the First Conditional through our 'Grammar Escape Room' to be able to explain scientific consequences.
Creative Design: Creating the visual menu using Canva, applying everything we learned about sensory marketing.
Final Showcase: Presenting our menus to the class and receiving peer feedback.
Check the timeline below to see the tasks for each session.

Organization is the secret ingredient of every great scientist!

odeComponent.htmlView:
🟢 Session 1: The Sensory Lab (Research Phase)
"What will we do?" In this first session, you will work in pairs to investigate the fascinating connection between biology and marketing. Using our collaborative Padlet, you must find out how the brain perceives the five basic tastes and, specifically, how certain colours (like blue or red) can trick our appetite.

Goal: Collect at least 3 scientific facts to justify your future menu choices.
Digital Tool: Padlet & Shared Google Doc for note-taking.


🔵 Session 2: The Grammar Escape (Language Mastery)
"What will we do?" Science needs precise language. To explain the 'cause and effect' of sensory marketing, we need the First Conditional. You will work in small teams to solve the riddles of 'The Grammar Escape' Genially. If you solve the puzzles, you will master the structure: 'If I use warm colours, customers will feel hungrier'.

Goal: Complete the Escape Room and obtain the secret code.
Digital Tool: Genially.


🟠 Sessions 3 & 4: Menu Creation (Creative Phase)
"What will we do?" It’s time to be creative! Using Canva, you will design a 3-course sensory menu. You must apply the psychology of colour to the design and write descriptions for each dish using the First Conditional. You need to justify why you chose those ingredients and those specific colours for your brand.

Goal: Design a professional digital menu.
Digital Tool: Canva.


🔴 Session 5: Food Critic Summit (Evaluation Phase)
"What will we do?" In the final session, we will act as professional food critics. You will present your menu to the 'Great Group' and perform peer evaluation. You will provide constructive feedback to your classmates based on their scientific accuracy and design.

Goal: Peer-assess and reflect on the learning process.
Digital Tool: Google Forms.

odeComponent.htmlView:
📝 Final Challenge: Self-Assessment & Project Reflection
"To successfully conclude our 'Savoury Science' journey, we will undergo a reflection process on what we have learned and how we have performed. This final questionnaire allows you to connect scientific and linguistic concepts with the creative decisions you made during the design of your menu.

What areas will be assessed?

Scientific & Linguistic Knowledge: You will justify your use of colour based on psychology, identify the Umami taste in your dishes, and correctly apply the First Conditional in a real-world context.
Digital Competence & Ethics: You will reflect on the design tools used (Canva) and the importance of using images with open licenses (Creative Commons).
Metacognition: You will evaluate your level of effort and your ability to improve, analyzing which steps of the process you would perform differently next time.


Instructions:

Answer each question in detail; your justifications are the key to the final assessment.
Be honest in your self-evaluation and critical reflection.
Do not forget to click the 'Submit' button at the end to ensure your responses are recorded.


Your ability to reflect is what truly makes you a great scientist and communicator!

odeComponent.htmlView:
How is your final menu graded? To help you achieve the best possible results, we use an Analytic Rubric. This document outlines exactly what we are looking for in your final project, from scientific accuracy to digital ethics.

How to use this rubric:

Before you submit: Check your work against the 'Sobresaliente (4)' column. Does your menu explain the 5 basic tastes? Is your typography justified?
Self-Check: Make sure you have used the First Conditional for offers and that all your images are properly attributed.
Continuous Improvement: Use the descriptions in the 'Notable' or 'Aprobado' columns to identify what you need to fix to reach the next level.
Key Evaluation Areas:

Taste Science: Strategic integration of the 5 tastes (including Umami).
Color Psychology: Professional justification of your visual palette.
Grammar Accuracy: Natural use of conditional structures.
Sensory Vocabulary: Use of specific technical terms.
Digital Ethics: Correct attribution and use of Creative Commons licenses.


Excellence is not an act, but a habit. Use this guide to polish your masterpiece!

Información general sobre este recurso educativo
Title Savouring Science
Description La unidad se divide en tres fases que integran la competencia digital de forma progresiva: 1. Fase Analítica (Reading & Logic): Investigación de la ciencia del gusto y psicología del color a través de distintos recursos recogidos en un Padlet. 2. Fase de Aplicación (Gamificación): Participación en el Escape Room interactivo de Genially. Aquí, los alumnos usan los condicionales para resolver misiones y desbloquear el mapa. 3. Fase Creativa (Writing): Creación de un "Sensory Menu". Utilizando una plantilla digital o física, diseñan tres platos, ponen nombre a su restaurante y justifican sus elecciones sensoriales empleando el First Conditional (ej: "If I play loud music, the food will taste less salty").
Authorship Alberto Millán Mielgo
License creative commons: attribution - non commercial - share alike 4.0

This content was created with eXeLearning, your free and open source editor to create educational resources.

Descargar recurso

1. Contextualización
Esta Situación de Aprendizaje (SdA) está diseñada para la materia de Lengua Extranjera: Inglés (3º o 4º de la ESO). El proyecto propone un enfoque interdisciplinar que une la Neurociencia del gusto y la Psicología del color con la producción lingüística en lengua inglesa.

2. Elementos Curriculares
El desarrollo de este proyecto garantiza el trabajo de las siguientes Competencias Específicas:

Producción y Comprensión (CE.1 y CE.3): El alumnado debe procesar información científica sobre el gusto y producir un menú atractivo utilizando el First Conditional.
Alfabetización Informacional (CE.4): Uso de herramientas de curación (Padlet/Wakelet) y respeto a los derechos de autor.
Competencia Digital (CD): Creación de contenidos mediante diseño gráfico ético y seguro.
Para ver cómo se vinculan las distintas actividades con los criterios de evaluación paso a paso, consulta el siguiente apartado: Criterios de evaluación

3. Atención a la Diversidad (Principios DUA)
Este recurso ha sido editado siguiendo las pautas del Diseño Universal para el Aprendizaje:

Múltiples formas de representación: La información se ofrece de forma visual, interactiva (Genially) y textual.
Múltiples formas de acción y expresión: El alumnado puede demostrar su competencia de forma creativa mediante el diseño visual en Canva.
Múltiples formas de implicación: La temática real y el componente de gamificación aumentan la motivación intrínseca.


4. Recomendaciones para el Profesorado
Herramientas: Consulte el Wakelet (en el nodo de Recursos Docentes) para acceder al repositorio de herramientas que sustentan este proyecto.
Seguridad: Es fundamental revisar con los alumnos la Infografía de Seguridad Digital incluida en este REA antes de comenzar la fase de diseño.
Evaluación: Se recomienda compartir la rúbrica de evaluación con los alumnos al inicio de la Sesión 3 para fomentar la autorregulación.

This Escape Room is a comprehensive review of the English conditional system. To succeed in the project, you must demonstrate your ability to use these structures with precision, as they are essential for scientific reasoning and hypothetical thinking.

What will you practice?

Zero Conditional: For universal truths and scientific facts.
First Conditional: For real possibilities and future results.
Second Conditional: For hypothetical or imaginary situations.
Third Conditional: For reflecting on past events and missed opportunities.


Instructions:

Interact: Explore the screens to find the hidden grammar puzzles.
Solve: Apply the correct conditional form to unlock the next stage.
Achievement: Reaching the final screen confirms you have the linguistic level required for the final phase of 'Savoury Science'.
Check your tenses, survivor. One wrong 'if' could change everything!

odeComponent.htmlView:
OVERVIEW: It’s time to apply your "Sensory Scientist" skills to a real-world product. You are going to design a 3-course digital menu that is not only delicious but also scientifically designed to attract customers.

📝 The Menu Requirements
Your final design must include:

- A Brand Name & Logo: Based on the color psychology researched in Session 1.
- Three Courses: Starter, Main Course, and Dessert.
- Sensory Descriptions: Each dish needs a short description explaining the flavors and textures.
- The "Scientific Why": Under each dish, you must include a sentence using the First Conditional to justify your design choices. Example: "If I use a yellow background for the dessert, customers will feel more energetic and happy."


🏃‍♂️ Step-by-Step Instructions
Step 1 - Draft your ideas: Write down the names of your dishes and the colors you will use.
Step 2 - Open Canva: Choose a "Menu" template. Remember: the layout and colors must match your brand's goal (e.g., healthy, fast food, luxury). Remember that in the section called "Design your Menu (Tutoriales)" within the Padlet you will find a Canva Tutorial and some Menus ideas. You can access the Padlet here. 
Step 3 - Design & Write: Insert high-quality images and write your descriptions. Make sure your First Conditional sentences are grammatically correct!
Step 4 - Export: Save your menu as a PDF or a Public Link to share it in the next session.

🎯 Goal
Design a professional digital menu that uses sensory marketing to influence consumer behavior.


Checklist: Before finishing, check that you have used at least 3 First Conditional sentences.

odeComponent.htmlView:
OVERVIEW: Welcome to the final stage! Today, you are no longer designers; you are Professional Food Critics. You will present your work, discuss your classmates' projects, and reflect on your own learning journey.

🍱 The Showcase
Each person will have 3 minutes to present their digital menu to the "Great Group". During the presentation, you must:

Explain the color psychology behind your brand.
Read your First Conditional sentences aloud.
Answer questions from the "critics" (your classmates).


🏃‍♂️ Step-by-Step Instructions
Present: Open your Canva menu and show your design to the class.
Debate: Engage in a class discussion about which menus were the most "persuasive" and why.
Self-Assessment: Open the "Savoury Science Self-Reflection Form" (Google Forms).
Reflect: Answer the questions honestly.


🎯 Goal
To reflect on the learning process and assess your own progress in English and Science.

🛠 Digital Tool
Self-Assessment Form Link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1C6Y8uToqpq7yx_zg7jBpoaJSJXioTv5VFGj902Ac43g/printform
